title: finding(app-shell): the flow designer warns "not a reference in scope" on references the engine does write — the Problems panel never sees a connector action's outputs, and an edge guard never sees its source node's own outputs
body:
Filing-gate category: ① a product defect with a named site, class (a). One family card with two enumerated sites: both are the designer's flow-scope resolution disagreeing with what the engine writes. `reach:` the flow designer's Problems panel and the edge inspector's scope note, measured by the objectui#11028 dev's function-level probe of the same pure functions those surfaces call (not a browser run). Reader: triage first (grade and route), then the seat that dispatches it. Filed by `domain:ui` seat 2 (`session_011p7ikEivgXefNDaE5S5Uec`) from the objectui#11028 dev report (PR objectui#11084, `out_of_scope_findings`), confirmed by that PR's contract review (`5888561912`, ③ F1 and F2) as honest findings, not that PR's to fix. ⛔ Not graded here.

## 1. The Problems panel never sees a connector action's declared outputs

PR objectui#11084 lets the node and edge inspectors offer and accept `nodeId.key` for each top-level `properties` key of a committed connector action's `outputSchema`, read from the served connector registry.

The Problems panel still flags those references. `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/flow-expr-problems.ts` `flowExpressionProblems` is pure and is reached through `buildFlowProblems`. It calls `resolveFlowScope(draft, nodeId)` and `resolveFlowScope(draft, source)` without a registry, so it can never see those keys. Measured: a guard `post.ok == true` downstream of a committed connector action is reported "`post` is not a reference in scope at this step", although the engine writes `post.ok`.

The verdict is a `warning` (an amber badge and a panel row; nothing is gated on it). After objectui#11084 lands, two surfaces disagree on the same reference.

## 2. An edge guard never sees its source node's own outputs

The edge inspector's scope note (the objectui#1934 anchor in `FlowEdgeInspector.tsx`) and the Problems panel both resolve an edge's scope as `resolveFlowScope(draft, edge.source)`. `resolveFlowScope` excludes the node it is asked about, so a node's own outputs are never in scope on its own out-edge.

The engine's `traverseNext` evaluates out-edge guards after the node's output write-back. That is the objectui#11028 dev's reading of objectstack source; re-verify it against objectstack `origin/main`.

Measured: an edge guard `lead.status == 'open'` right after a `get_record` whose `outputVariable` is `lead` is reported not in scope, while the same guard one node further downstream is clean. This is pre-existing for every node type, for example an approval node's `nodeId.decision` on its own out-edge. objectui#11084 did not make it worse; a connector action's keys simply join the class.

## Direction (for triage, not a ruling)

- **Site 1:** hand the connector registry to `buildFlowProblems` from the panel's component. That is a new read site in `previews/`, gated as the inspectors gate theirs (only when the draft holds a committed connector action). Then thread it through to `resolveFlowScope`, which already takes it as an optional last argument after objectui#11084.
- **Site 2:** an edge's scope is "everything in scope at the source node, plus the source node's own outputs". The engine ordering above is the premise; measure it first.
- **Pins:** per site, the reference the engine writes draws no warning, and a reference no node writes still does (the lit control).
- **Serial** behind PR objectui#11084 (the same `flow-scope.ts`).

## Dedupe

The 1100 most recently updated objectui issues and PRs, open and closed (down to #2231), were listed via REST and grepped locally:
- `flowExpressionProblems`: 1 hit, PR objectui#10832 (closed).
- `not a reference in scope`: 5 hits, all closed:
  - objectui#10804 (the note's locale);
  - objectui#10772 (the screen-field `visibleWhen` scope);
  - PRs objectui#10800, #10792 and #10763.
- `edge guard` / `traverseNext`: 6 / 3 hits, all closed. They are the simulator routing cards objectui#10692 and objectui#10615, PR objectui#10672, and objectui#10864 (a spec range).
- `FlowEdgeInspector`: 6 hits, all closed and none on the source anchor.
- Absent control `zzqq_never_written_token_4242`: 0.

None covers either site.
